items: Severe constant pain, vomiting, tenderness, ileus; chronic disease adds steatorrhea and weight loss
★ **Hypoxemia, hypotension, oliguria, persistent SIRS** → early monitored/ICU assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Premature intrapancreatic enzyme activation → autodigestion and systemic inflammation
Chronic fibrosis destroys acinar/islet tissue; lipase may normalize despite advanced disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Acute diagnosis: **2 of 3**—typical pain, lipase ≥3× ULN, characteristic imaging
RUQ ultrasound evaluates gallstones; triglycerides, calcium, liver tests identify cause
Contrast CT for uncertain diagnosis, deterioration, or failure to improve after 48–72 hours; not routine immediately
Chronic: CT/MRCP shows calcification/duct changes; fecal elastase <200 supports exocrine insufficiency

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute: **moderate lactated Ringer resuscitation**, frequent reassessment, analgesia, electrolyte correction; avoid overload
★ **Early oral low-fat feeding** within 24–48 hours if tolerated; enteral tube feeding if unable
Biliary with cholangitis → urgent ERCP; mild gallstone disease → cholecystectomy before discharge
Sterile necrosis: no antibiotics; infected: penetrating antibiotics, delayed step-up drainage/debridement
Chronic: stop alcohol/tobacco; pancreatic enzymes, nutrition/fat-soluble vitamins, pain and diabetes management

rows.label: Complications
items: ARDS, AKI, shock, hypocalcemia; local necrosis, vascular thrombosis, hemorrhage
Pseudocyst after >4 weeks; infected collection, obstruction; chronic disease → pancreatic cancer and brittle diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Treat cause**: gallbladder removal, triglyceride control, avoid culprit drug and alcohol
Post-ERCP rectal indomethacin in eligible patients; selected pancreatic duct stenting

rows.label: Mimics
items: Perforated ulcer: rigid abdomen/free air
Mesenteric ischemia: pain-exam mismatch; MI: ischemic ECG/troponin pattern

table.title: Severity and collections
rows: Transient dysfunction ≤48 hours or local complication

perioperative-care.name: Perioperative care
perioperative-care.scope: Preoperative cardiac risk, pulmonary evaluation, surgical antibiotic prophylaxis, medication management, pain control
perioperative-care.core: Optimize active disease, estimate procedural and patient risk, and order testing only when the result could change perioperative management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Emergency, vascular or intrathoracic surgery; ischemic heart disease, heart failure, CKD, diabetes
Smoking, COPD, OSA, frailty, malnutrition and prior anesthesia complications

rows.label: Clues
items: Chest pain, new dyspnea, syncope or decompensated fluid overload require targeted evaluation
Poor functional capacity: inability to climb stairs or perform activities around 4 METs

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Surgical stress raises myocardial oxygen demand; anesthesia can lower perfusion pressure
Sedation, pain and recumbency reduce ventilation and promote atelectasis and venous stasis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **RCRI/NSQIP** plus functional assessment; no routine stress test for low-risk surgery
Selected elevated-risk surgery with poor/unknown capacity → stress test only if results change management
ECG for cardiovascular symptoms; echo for new/worsening HF or suspected significant valve disease
No routine chest radiograph/spirometry without respiratory findings; assess airway and OSA history

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Active ACS, decompensated HF or unstable arrhythmia → defer elective surgery and stabilize
★ Continue chronic **beta blockers/statins**; do not start beta blockade on surgery day
Hold **SGLT2 inhibitors 3–4 days**; individualize GLP-1 drugs by aspiration risk; continue reduced basal insulin
★ **Cefazolin within 60 minutes** before incision; vancomycin infusion starts within 120 minutes
Multimodal analgesia: acetaminophen, regional block, selective NSAID; opioids for breakthrough, respiratory monitoring

rows.label: Complications
items: Myocardial injury, AKI, delirium, pneumonia, VTE and surgical-site infection
Opioids aggravate OSA; excessive fluids can worsen pulmonary edema

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, lung expansion exercises, early mobilization, mechanical/pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis
Anticoagulation interruption individualized; bridging reserved for highest thrombotic risk
Chronic steroid exposure with adrenal suppression → perioperative glucocorticoid coverage

rows.label: Mimics
items: Anxiety-related dyspnea: normal cardiopulmonary evaluation
Stable chronic disease: baseline symptoms alone do not mandate cancellation

peripheral-artery-disease.name: Peripheral artery disease
peripheral-artery-disease.scope: Claudication, aortoiliac (Leriche) disease, critical and acute limb ischemia
peripheral-artery-disease.core: Atherosclerotic limb hypoperfusion ranges from exertional claudication to rest pain, tissue loss, or abrupt limb-threatening arterial occlusion.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, age, CKD, hypertension, dyslipidemia; coronary/cerebrovascular atherosclerosis commonly coexists
AF, aneurysm, graft disease, hypercoagulability predispose acute occlusion

rows.label: Clues
items: Diminished pulses, cool shiny skin, hair loss, dependent rubor, distal nonhealing ulcers
★ **Pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesia, paralysis, poikilothermia** → acute limb ischemia
Sensory/motor deficits signal threatened limb; do not await all six findings

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fixed arterial narrowing limits exercise perfusion; progressive failure reduces resting tissue oxygenation
Acute embolus/thrombus prevents collateral compensation, rapidly injuring nerves and muscle

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ABI ≤0.90** confirms PAD; 0.91–0.99 borderline; >1.40 suggests noncompressible arteries
Exertional symptoms with normal resting ABI → exercise ABI; noncompressible vessels → toe-brachial index
Duplex, CTA/MRA define anatomy when revascularization planned; urgent Doppler exam in acute ischemia

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic PAD: **clopidogrel or aspirin + high-intensity statin**, smoking cessation, structured exercise
Cilostazol improves claudication; contraindicated in any heart failure
Refractory disabling claudication → revascularization; chronic limb-threatening ischemia → prompt limb-salvage evaluation
★ Acute ischemia → **IV unfractionated heparin and immediate vascular consultation**; salvageable limb → urgent reperfusion
Low bleeding risk, symptomatic/postrevascularization → low-dose rivaroxaban + aspirin; no full anticoagulation solely for PAD

rows.label: Complications
items: Gangrene, infection, amputation; MI/stroke often dominate long-term mortality
Reperfusion → compartment syndrome, hyperkalemia, rhabdomyolysis; irreversible limb may require primary amputation

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Daily foot inspection**, protective footwear, diabetic foot care, BP/glucose control
Avoid thermal injury to insensate feet; antithrombotic plan after procedures based on bleeding risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Spinal stenosis: flexion relieves walking pain, pulses preserved
Venous ulcer: medial ankle, edema, pulses intact; neuropathy: sensory loss without ischemic pulse findings

table.title: Clinical stages
rows: Reproducible exercise pain relieved by rest
Buttock claudication, erectile dysfunction, weak femorals

pilonidal-disease.name: Pilonidal disease
pilonidal-disease.scope: Pilonidal cyst, acute pilonidal abscess, sinus tract with pits, incision and drainage, wound care, recurrence
pilonidal-disease.core: Acquired hair-driven inflammation in the natal cleft ranges from incidental pits to painful abscesses and chronically draining sinuses.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young adults, male sex, dense body hair, deep gluteal cleft, obesity
Prolonged sitting, friction, sweating; family predisposition and prior episodes increase recurrence

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Midline pits over the sacrococcygeal cleft**, sometimes containing hair/debris
Acute tender erythematous fluctuant swelling; drainage can arise through lateral openings
Recurrent serous/purulent discharge with induration suggests persistent sinus; systemic toxicity unusual in localized disease
Lesions close to anal verge or atypical openings → evaluate another diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Loose hairs penetrate cleft skin → foreign-body reaction and secondary infection
Persistent cavities/tracts permit repeated inflammation rather than representing a congenital spinal connection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical examination** of cleft and perianal region; imaging usually unnecessary
Assess fever, surrounding cellulitis, immunocompromise and extent of fluctuance
Atypical deep/recurrent disease near anus → MRI or colorectal evaluation for fistula/Crohn disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute abscess → **incision and drainage**; do not substitute oral antibiotics
Cellulitis → cephalexin ± TMP-SMX for MRSA risk; systemic toxicity/immunocompromise → hospital assessment
After drainage → analgesia, dressing changes and cleansing; reassess wound healing
★ Persistent/recurrent symptomatic sinus → elective **excision or minimally invasive tract procedure**
Complex disease → off-midline flap/closure preferred over primary midline closure; asymptomatic pits generally observed

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent abscess, persistent sinus and drainage, delayed wound healing; extensive surgery may cause prolonged recovery
Repeated inflammation → scarring, impaired sitting/activity; postoperative wound dehiscence or infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Cleft hygiene, reduce retained hair/friction; consider laser hair removal, especially recurrent disease
Smoking cessation and weight management support healing; recurrence remains possible after any procedure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Epidermoid cyst: punctum away from characteristic cleft pits
Furuncle: isolated infected follicle without persistent sinus system

table.title: Other anogenital sinus disorders
rows: External opening connects toward anal canal

renal-cell-carcinoma.name: Renal cell carcinoma
renal-cell-carcinoma.scope: Clear cell RCC, classic triad (hematuria, flank pain, palpable mass), paraneoplastic syndromes (hypercalcemia, erythrocytosis, fever), CT abdomen, nephrectomy
renal-cell-carcinoma.core: An enhancing solid renal mass is malignant until evaluated; RCC may present incidentally or through systemic manifestations before urinary symptoms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, obesity, hypertension; acquired cystic kidney disease in long-term dialysis
Von Hippel–Lindau syndrome: bilateral/multifocal clear cell tumors; younger age prompts hereditary evaluation

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Painless **hematuria**; classic hematuria–flank pain–palpable mass triad is uncommon and suggests advanced disease
Weight loss, fever, anemia; new nonreducible left varicocele suggests renal vein involvement
Hypercalcemia from PTHrP; erythrocytosis from EPO; hypertension from renin
Stauffer syndrome: reversible hepatic dysfunction without liver metastases

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Clear cell tumor from proximal tubular epithelium; lipid/glycogen-rich cytoplasm
VHL loss → HIF accumulation, VEGF-driven angiogenesis; propensity for renal vein/IVC invasion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Renal-protocol **contrast CT abdomen/pelvis** characterizes enhancement and stages local disease
MRI if venous invasion uncertain or CT unsuitable; chest imaging evaluates lung spread
CBC, creatinine, calcium, liver tests; urinalysis confirms blood but cannot exclude tumor
Biopsy before ablation/systemic treatment or when management uncertain; unnecessary before clearly indicated resection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized small tumor → **partial nephrectomy** when feasible, especially solitary kidney or CKD
Large/complex localized tumor → radical nephrectomy; remove venous tumor thrombus when operable
Small mass in frail patient → active surveillance or thermal ablation after individualized assessment
★ Advanced disease → immune checkpoint combinations, e.g., pembrolizumab/axitinib or nivolumab/ipilimumab
Selected high-risk resected clear cell disease → adjuvant pembrolizumab; conventional cytotoxic chemotherapy poorly effective

rows.label: Complications
items: Lung, bone, liver, brain metastases; pathologic fractures, venous obstruction
Nephrectomy: reduced renal reserve; immunotherapy: immune-mediated organ injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Smoking cessation, weight management, blood pressure control; no population-wide imaging screening
Hereditary syndromes → genetic counseling and renal surveillance; follow postoperative renal function and recurrence

rows.label: Mimics
items: Angiomyolipoma: macroscopic fat on CT; can hemorrhage
Simple renal cyst: thin wall, homogeneous fluid, no enhancement
Urothelial carcinoma: collecting-system origin; urine cytology may help

sarcoidosis.name: Sarcoidosis
sarcoidosis.scope: Noncaseating granulomas, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, pulmonary infiltrates, hypercalcemia, extrapulmonary manifestations (uveitis, erythema nodosum, neurosarcoidosis, cardiac), systemic corticosteroids
sarcoidosis.core: Multisystem granulomatous disease, classically a young adult with bilateral hilar adenopathy; treat threatened organ function rather than an abnormal radiograph alone.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young or middle-aged adults; higher prevalence and disease burden among Black Americans
Familial predisposition; environmental antigen exposure suspected, without one established infectious cause

rows.label: Clues
items: Dry cough, exertional dyspnea; restrictive physiology and ↓DLCO; upper-lung interstitial infiltrates
★ **Löfgren syndrome**: erythema nodosum + ankle arthritis + hilar adenopathy; usually favorable prognosis
Uveitis, lupus pernio, parotid enlargement; facial palsy, hypothalamic dysfunction suggest neurosarcoidosis
★ Unexplained **AV block, ventricular arrhythmia, syncope** → cardiac involvement

rows.label: Pathophys
items: CD4-mediated granulomas; macrophage 1α-hydroxylase → ↑calcitriol, hypercalcemia/hypercalciuria, suppressed PTH

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Chest radiograph**, PFTs; baseline calcium, creatinine, liver tests, ECG and eye examination
Compatible presentation + **noncaseating granulomas** + exclusion of TB/fungi/beryllium exposure
Sample accessible lesion or EBUS-guided hilar/mediastinal node; classic Löfgren presentation may avoid biopsy
ACE level neither sensitive nor specific; cardiac symptoms/ECG abnormalities → cardiac MRI ± FDG-PET

rows.label: Tx
items: Asymptomatic stage I disease, preserved function → observation with clinical/PFT follow-up
★ **Prednisone** for progressive symptomatic pulmonary disease, significant hypercalcemia, cardiac or neurologic disease
Uveitis → urgent ophthalmology, topical or systemic corticosteroids according to severity
Steroid-dependent disease → methotrexate; refractory organ-threatening disease → specialist-directed infliximab
Hypercalcemia → hydration; restrict excess calcium/vitamin D and sunlight exposure

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary fibrosis, pulmonary hypertension, respiratory failure; nephrolithiasis and kidney injury
Cardiomyopathy, sudden death; visual loss; chronic steroids → infection, osteoporosis, diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: No established primary prevention; smoking cessation and vaccination reduce respiratory morbidity
Monitor treatment toxicity and bone health; individualize vitamin D replacement because calcitriol may already be elevated

rows.label: Mimics
items: TB/fungal infection: organisms or positive microbiology; exclude before immunosuppression
Berylliosis: aerospace/industrial exposure, positive beryllium lymphocyte proliferation test
Lymphoma: malignant tissue, constitutional symptoms; granulomas alone do not exclude concurrent cancer

secondary-hypertension.name: Secondary hypertension
secondary-hypertension.scope: Renal artery stenosis, primary hyperaldosteronism, pheochromocytoma, Cushing syndrome, coarctation of aorta, diagnostic workup
secondary-hypertension.core: Abrupt, unusually young, severe, or resistant hypertension suggests a treatable secondary driver.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Atherosclerosis, fibromuscular dysplasia, renal disease, adrenal tumors, sleep apnea
NSAIDs, oral contraceptives, stimulants, glucocorticoids, licorice; medication nonadherence can mimic resistance

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Hypokalemia** suggests mineralocorticoid excess but normal K does not exclude it
Flash pulmonary edema or creatinine rise >30% after ACE inhibitor/ARB → renovascular disease
Endocrine spells, cushingoid appearance, or upper-body hypertension guide cause-specific testing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Renal hypoperfusion activates RAAS; mineralocorticoid signaling increases distal sodium absorption and potassium loss
Catecholamine/cortisol excess, aortic obstruction, or nocturnal hypoxia increases vascular pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm **home/ambulatory BP**, adherence, cuff technique; BMP, urinalysis, creatinine, TSH
Sleep-apnea symptoms → polysomnography; abnormal urinary sediment → renal ultrasound and kidney evaluation
★ Biochemical testing precedes adrenal imaging; correct hypokalemia and account for interfering medications
Endocrine Society 2025: suggest **aldosterone screening for all hypertension**, conditional on resources

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Primary aldosteronism: unilateral → **adrenalectomy**; bilateral → spironolactone/eplerenone
Renovascular atherosclerosis → medical risk reduction; revascularize selected recurrent pulmonary edema or refractory disease
Fibromuscular dysplasia → angioplasty; critical bilateral renal stenosis → avoid ACE inhibitor/ARB
★ Pheochromocytoma: **alpha blockade before beta blockade**, volume expansion, then surgery
Treat cortisol source, repair significant coarctation, use CPAP for OSA; stop contributing drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, heart failure, CKD, retinopathy
Unopposed alpha stimulation after beta blockade can cause catecholamine crisis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor renal function/K after RAAS blockers or mineralocorticoid antagonists
Genetic evaluation/family screening for suspected hereditary pheochromocytoma or congenital aortic disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: normal out-of-office readings
Essential hypertension: gradual course without specific endocrine/renal clues

table.title: Targeted workup
rows: Selective suppression test; CT/adrenal venous sampling
Plasma free or urine fractionated metanephrines

secondary-hypertension.evidence: Aldosterone screening checked 2026-10-30: [Endocrine Society 2025](https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/primary-aldosteronism-2); other causes: established teaching.

shock.name: Shock
shock.scope: Hypovolemic, cardiogenic, distributive (septic, anaphylactic, neurogenic), obstructive, fluid resuscitation, vasopressors
shock.core: Circulatory failure causing tissue hypoperfusion; normal blood pressure does not exclude early shock.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hemorrhage, GI losses, MI, infection, allergen exposure, spinal injury, thromboembolism
Recent surgery, immunosuppression, indwelling devices increase occult infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Tachycardia, altered mentation, oliguria, cool mottled skin; distributive forms may initially feel warm
★ **Anaphylaxis**: rapid airway swelling, wheezing, hypotension; skin findings may be absent
Neurogenic: hypotension with **bradycardia**, warm skin after spinal cord injury

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Oxygen delivery falls below demand → anaerobic metabolism, lactate accumulation
Distributive vasodilation → relative hypovolemia despite normal total body fluid

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Bedside ultrasound**: cardiac function, pericardial fluid, RV dilation, lung sliding, volume assessment
Serial lactate, capillary refill, urine output; CBC, chemistry, ECG, troponin; cultures if infection suspected
Septic shock: vasopressors for MAP ≥65 plus lactate >2 despite volume resuscitation

rows.label: Tx
items: Airway/oxygen, IV access; **balanced crystalloid**, dynamic fluid-response reassessment; restrict with pulmonary congestion
★ Hemorrhage → **control bleeding + balanced blood products**; avoid large crystalloid loads
★ Septic shock → antibiotics within 1 hour, drainage/debridement; crystalloid 30 mL/kg within 3 hours
★ Persistent septic hypotension → **norepinephrine**, MAP ≥65; add vasopressin, then epinephrine; refractory → hydrocortisone

rows.label: Complications
items: AKI, ischemic hepatitis, DIC, ARDS, bowel ischemia, multiorgan failure
Excess fluids → edema; vasopressors → digital/mesenteric ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early infection treatment, catheter hygiene, VTE prophylaxis, hemorrhage control
After anaphylaxis: trigger avoidance, epinephrine autoinjector, allergy referral

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vasovagal syncope: transient bradycardia, rapid recovery supine
Hypoglycemia: low bedside glucose, improvement with dextrose

table.title: Hemodynamics and cause-directed rescue
rows: Decompress pneumothorax; drain tamponade; reperfuse PE

small-intestinal-bacterial-overgrowth.name: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth
small-intestinal-bacterial-overgrowth.scope: Etiologies (surgical blind loop, strictures, motility disorders), breath testing, quantitative jejunal culture, oral antibiotics (rifaximin, amoxicillin-clavulanate)
small-intestinal-bacterial-overgrowth.core: Bloating and malabsorption in a patient with small-bowel stasis suggest excessive luminal bacteria; address the underlying cause as well as bacterial burden.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Surgical blind loop**, small-bowel diverticula, strictures, altered anatomy, ileocecal valve resection
Dysmotility: systemic sclerosis, diabetic autonomic neuropathy, chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction
Achlorhydria or impaired host defenses increase susceptibility; PPI exposure alone does not establish diagnosis

rows.label: Clues
items: Postprandial distention, flatulence, diarrhea; severe disease causes steatorrhea and weight loss
★ **Low B12 with normal/high folate** suggests bacterial consumption and folate synthesis
Fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies; methane-associated overgrowth often accompanies constipation rather than diarrhea

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Bacterial deconjugation of bile acids → impaired micelles and fat malabsorption
Carbohydrate fermentation → gas; bacterial nutrient competition and mucosal injury impair absorption

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Symptomatic at-risk patient → **glucose or lactulose hydrogen breath test**; interpret with clinical context
Hydrogen rise ≥20 ppm above baseline by 90 minutes supports SIBO
Small-bowel aspirate culture: ≥10^3 CFU/mL accepted current threshold; classic teaching often uses ≥10^5
Methane ≥10 ppm → intestinal methanogen overgrowth, not strictly bacterial or exclusively small-intestinal
Rapid transit causes false positives, especially lactulose; glucose may miss distal overgrowth; testing imperfect

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Oral **rifaximin** or amoxicillin-clavulanate; short course, commonly 10–14 days
Replete B12 and other deficiencies; provide nutritional support if weight loss significant
Correct obstructing stricture/blind loop when feasible; manage dysmotility and reduce motility-impairing drugs
Recurrent symptoms → reassess cause and diagnosis before repeated antibiotics; no universal eradication regimen

rows.label: Complications
items: Malnutrition, B12-related neuropathy, fat-soluble vitamin deficiency, osteomalacia
Antibiotics: resistance, adverse reactions, C difficile infection; recurrence common if stasis persists

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Optimize motility and surgically correct relevant anatomy; avoid unnecessary acid suppression
Long-term restrictive diets or probiotics lack established universal preventive benefit

rows.label: Mimics
items: Celiac disease: positive tissue transglutaminase IgA, villous atrophy
Pancreatic insufficiency: low fecal elastase, pancreatitis history
IBS: no objective nutritional deficiency or malabsorption; overlap possible

thoracic-trauma.name: Thoracic trauma
thoracic-trauma.scope: Blunt and penetrating chest trauma, blunt cardiac injury, blunt aortic injury, diaphragmatic rupture, pulmonary contusion
thoracic-trauma.core: Chest trauma with respiratory or circulatory compromise requires immediate treatment of life-threatening injuries before definitive imaging.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: High-speed deceleration, steering-wheel impact, crush injuries, penetrating wounds
Lower chest wounds can cross diaphragm and injure abdominal organs

rows.label: Clues
items: Unilateral absent breath sounds, shock, distended neck veins → tension pneumothorax
Flail segment: paradoxical movement; associated lung injury drives hypoxemia
Delayed respiratory deterioration after blunt impact → pulmonary contusion
Left thoracic bowel sounds or elevated hemidiaphragm → diaphragmatic rupture

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pleural pressure or pericardial blood impairs venous return → obstructive shock
Alveolar hemorrhage and edema impair gas exchange; rapid deceleration shears the aortic isthmus

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Primary survey with **eFAST** and portable chest radiograph; unstable injuries treated clinically
★ Suspected aortic injury, stable → **CT angiography**; normal radiograph cannot exclude
Blunt cardiac injury → ECG and troponin; both normal effectively exclude significant injury
New arrhythmia or elevated troponin → telemetry; persistent shock → echocardiography

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Tension pneumothorax → immediate needle/finger decompression → **chest tube**; no imaging delay
Open pneumothorax → vented seal and tube; hemothorax → tube and blood resuscitation
★ Initial tube blood >1500 mL or persistent >200 mL/h → operative exploration
Tamponade with shock/arrest → surgical drainage; pericardiocentesis only temporizing
Contusion/flail chest → oxygen, regional/multimodal analgesia, pulmonary hygiene; intubate for respiratory failure

rows.label: Complications
items: Contusion → ARDS; retained hemothorax → empyema
Rib fractures → splinting, atelectasis, pneumonia; cardiac injury → arrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Seat belts, vehicle safety systems and protective equipment reduce injury risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cardiogenic shock: ventricular dysfunction without pericardial compression
Abdominal hemorrhage: free intraperitoneal fluid; may coexist with thoracic injury

thoracic-trauma.evidence: Not checked online; established ATLS-based teaching.

table.title: Definitive associated-injury management
rows: IV esmolol if tolerated; endovascular repair

thrombocytopenia.name: Thrombocytopenia
thrombocytopenia.scope: Evaluation of isolated thrombocytopenia, peripheral smear, immune thrombocytopenia, drug-induced, procedural platelet thresholds
thrombocytopenia.core: Low platelet count requires confirmation and distinction among impaired production, immune destruction, consumption, sequestration, and laboratory artifact.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent infection, autoimmune disease, HIV/HCV, lymphoproliferative disease → secondary immune thrombocytopenia
Heparin, quinine, TMP-SMX, vancomycin; alcohol, marrow-suppressive drugs; cirrhosis with splenic sequestration

rows.label: Clues
items: Petechiae, purpura, epistaxis, gingival bleeding; mucosal hemorrhage signals clinically important platelet disorder
★ **Neurologic/renal abnormalities + hemolysis** → thrombotic microangiopathy; systemic illness/coagulopathy → DIC
Heparin exposure + >50% platelet decline, thrombosis, typical 5–10-day onset → HIT

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ITP: IgG-mediated platelet clearance and impaired megakaryocyte production
Drug-dependent immune destruction often causes abrupt severe counts; HIT activates platelets, producing thrombosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Repeat CBC + peripheral smear**; platelet clumps → citrate tube for pseudothrombocytopenia
Isolated low platelets, normal coagulation, large platelets → ITP after excluding secondary causes
Schistocytes → LDH, haptoglobin, creatinine, coagulation studies; suspected TTP → urgent ADAMTS13 sample
HIV/HCV testing for new ITP; marrow biopsy only atypical cytopenias or suspected marrow disease
4Ts estimates HIT probability; intermediate/high → PF4 immunoassay, functional confirmation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Adult ITP **<30,000/µL or bleeding → glucocorticoid**; children without significant bleeding → observation
★ ITP critical bleeding → **IVIG + high-dose steroid + platelet transfusion**
Drug immune thrombocytopenia → stop culprit; persistent ITP → rituximab, thrombopoietin agonist, or selected splenectomy
Suspected TTP → plasma exchange; HIT → stop heparin, start argatroban/nonheparin anticoagulant
Older board LP target: 50,000/µL; current trigger below; neurosurgical targets often ≥100,000/µL

rows.label: Complications
items: Intracranial hemorrhage with severe disease; thrombosis in HIT/TTP
Steroid toxicity, immunosuppression; splenectomy → encapsulated bacterial sepsis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid culprit rechallenge, aspirin/NSAIDs when bleeding risk high; vaccinate before splenectomy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Von Willebrand disease: often normal platelet count with mucocutaneous bleeding
Marrow failure: additional cytopenias, abnormal precursor morphology

thrombocytopenia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AABB/ICTMG platelet recommendations (2025)](https://www.aabb.org/news-resources/news/article/2025/05/29/aabb-develops-new-platelet-transfusion-guidelines); other hematology principles not separately checked.

transfusion-reactions.name: Transfusion reactions
transfusion-reactions.scope: Acute hemolytic, febrile nonhemolytic, TRALI, TACO, anaphylactic, delayed hemolytic, massive transfusion complications
transfusion-reactions.core: New symptoms during transfusion require stopping the transfusion immediately and evaluating hemolysis, infection and cardiopulmonary compromise.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior transfusion/pregnancy → alloantibodies; IgA deficiency with anti-IgA → anaphylaxis
Heart/kidney failure, rapid infusion, older age → circulatory overload

rows.label: Clues
items: Delayed hemolysis: hemoglobin falls with jaundice days–weeks after apparently compatible transfusion
Bacterial contamination: high fever, rigors, profound hypotension; platelets particularly vulnerable
Isolated urticaria without systemic symptoms suggests mild allergic reaction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ABO mismatch → complement-mediated intravascular lysis; anamnestic antibodies → delayed extravascular hemolysis
TRALI: inflammatory pulmonary capillary leak; TACO: hydrostatic pressure from excess circulating volume

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Keep IV access with saline; **recheck patient/unit identity**, notify blood bank
Hemolysis workup: DAT, LDH, bilirubin, haptoglobin, plasma/urine hemoglobin; send unit and blood samples
Fever/shock → patient and product cultures; dyspnea → chest radiograph, oxygenation, volume assessment
Suspected febrile nonhemolytic reaction remains diagnosis of exclusion after hemolysis/sepsis evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute hemolysis → IV saline, support renal perfusion, treat shock/DIC; **never restart unit**
★ Anaphylaxis → **IM epinephrine**, airway support; future washed or IgA-deficient products
TRALI → supportive oxygen/ventilation; diuretics generally unhelpful unless concomitant overload
TACO → upright positioning, oxygen, **IV furosemide**; slow future transfusions
Suspected contamination → broad IV antibiotics; mild isolated allergy → diphenhydramine after clinical reassessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute hemolysis → AKI, DIC; severe pulmonary reactions → respiratory failure
Massive transfusion → citrate hypocalcemia, hyperkalemia, hypothermia, dilutional thrombocytopenia/coagulopathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Bedside identification and crossmatch; leukoreduction reduces febrile reactions
Massive hemorrhage → balanced blood components, temperature and ionized calcium monitoring

rows.label: Mimics
items: Underlying sepsis: symptoms may precede infusion; cultures clarify
Aspiration: event-linked infiltrate without transfusion-specific mechanism

transfusion-reactions.evidence: Not checked online; established transfusion-medicine definitions.

traumatic-brain-injury.name: Traumatic brain injury
traumatic-brain-injury.scope: Epidural hematoma, subdural hematoma, cerebral contusion, diffuse axonal injury, concussion, elevated ICP
traumatic-brain-injury.core: Head trauma ranges from transient functional disturbance to expanding hemorrhage; serial neurologic deterioration requires urgent imaging and neurosurgical assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Falls, crashes, assault, sports; anticoagulation increases bleeding
Older age, alcohol use and cerebral atrophy predispose to bridging-vein injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Headache, vomiting, amnesia; focal deficit or progressive somnolence suggests structural injury
★ **Unilateral fixed dilated pupil + declining consciousness** → uncal herniation
Cushing response: hypertension, bradycardia, irregular breathing; late sign of critically elevated ICP

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impact/shear → secondary edema, ischemia, excitotoxicity
Rising intracranial volume → reduced cerebral perfusion; hypotension/hypoxia sharply worsen secondary injury

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ ABCs/cervical protection → **GCS, pupils, focal examination**, repeated serially
**Noncontrast head CT** for moderate/severe injury or mild injury with high-risk features
High-risk features: anticoagulation, skull-fracture signs, focal deficit, repeated vomiting, worsening symptoms
GCS 13–15 mild, 9–12 moderate, ≤8 severe; diffuse axonal injury may require MRI

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **GCS ≤8 → intubate** with spinal protection; prevent hypoxemia/hypotension; reverse anticoagulants promptly
Expanding hematoma, mass effect or deterioration → urgent neurosurgical evacuation; observation only with close monitoring
★ Elevated ICP → head elevation, analgesia/sedation, **hypertonic saline or mannitol**; treat sustained ICP >22 mm Hg
Herniation → brief hyperventilation as bridge; avoid routine prophylactic hyperventilation and corticosteroids
Severe/high-risk TBI → levetiracetam for 7 days; refractory ICP → neurosurgical decompression

rows.label: Complications
items: Posttraumatic seizures, chronic cognitive/behavioral impairment, postconcussion syndrome, hydrocephalus

rows.label: Mimics

Hypoglycemia: immediate glucose testing identifies reversible altered mental status

valvular-heart-disease.name: Valvular heart disease
valvular-heart-disease.scope: Aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation, mitral stenosis, mitral regurgitation, mitral valve prolapse, physical exam, echocardiography, surgical and transcatheter replacement
valvular-heart-disease.core: Murmur timing, location, radiation, and loading maneuvers localize valve disease; symptoms and ventricular response determine intervention.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Aging calcification/bicuspid valve → AS; rheumatic disease → MS
Endocarditis, aortic root dilation/dissection → AR; ischemia, prolapse, chamber dilation → MR

rows.label: Clues
items: Exertional dyspnea, pulmonary edema, reduced exercise tolerance; abrupt deterioration suggests acute regurgitation
★ **Exertional syncope, angina, or HF** with obstruction → severe symptomatic disease
Squatting/handgrip increase regurgitant murmurs; standing/Valsalva makes MVP click earlier

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stenosis produces upstream pressure overload; regurgitation produces chamber volume overload
Acute regurgitation lacks compensatory dilation, rapidly elevating filling pressures and reducing forward output

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TTE Doppler** defines anatomy, severity, EF, chamber dimensions, pulmonary pressures
Severe AS: velocity ≥4 m/s, mean gradient ≥40, or valve area ≤1 cm²; discordance requires reassessment
Severe MS: valve area ≤1.5 cm²; TEE for thrombus before balloon intervention or uncertain anatomy
★ Acute murmur with shock → **urgent echocardiography**; TEE if endocarditis/dissection suspected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute severe AR/MR → **urgent surgery**, stabilize with afterload reduction/diuresis if BP permits
Severe primary MR: **EF ≤60% or LVESD ≥40 mm** triggers intervention even without symptoms
Secondary MR → optimize HF treatment first; selected persistent severe cases benefit from transcatheter edge-to-edge repair
Avoid excessive preload reduction in severe AS; symptomatic relief never replaces needed valve intervention

rows.label: Complications
items: Heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, AF, systemic embolism, endocarditis
Mechanical prosthesis: thrombosis/bleeding; bioprosthesis: structural degeneration

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Warfarin for mechanical valves**; no DOAC substitution; rheumatic MS with AF also requires warfarin
Prosthetic valve or prior endocarditis → selected dental prophylaxis; native isolated MVP does not qualify
Periodic echo and symptom review; treat rheumatic fever to prevent recurrent valve injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: HCM: systolic murmur increases with Valsalva/standing
Aortic sclerosis: ejection murmur without significant gradient; flow murmur: normal valve anatomy

table.title: Valve signatures and definitive options
rows: Early diastolic decrescendo; wide pulse pressure
Suitable symptomatic rheumatic valve → balloon commissurotomy

venous-thromboembolism.name: Venous thromboembolism
venous-thromboembolism.core: Unilateral swollen leg or sudden unexplained dyspnea with pleuritic pain; pulmonary embolism severity determined by hemodynamics, not clot size.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Immobilization, surgery, malignancy, estrogen, pregnancy/postpartum, previous VTE, inherited thrombophilia

rows.label: Clues
items: DVT: asymmetric calf tenderness, warmth; PE: tachycardia, hypoxemia, hemoptysis, sometimes normal oxygen saturation
Syncope, elevated JVP, cool extremities → impending RV failure; normal chest radiograph does not exclude PE

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stasis/endothelial injury/hypercoagulability → venous clot; pulmonary obstruction → V/Q mismatch, RV pressure overload

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Wells/pretest probability** first; very low-risk + PERC-negative → no testing
★ Low/intermediate probability → **D-dimer**; negative excludes; positive/high probability → **CT pulmonary angiography**
Age >50: D-dimer threshold age × 10 ng/mL FEU; contrast contraindication → V/Q scan
DVT → compression US; negative proximal scan + persistent suspicion → repeat in 1 week

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Oxygen/support circulation; unstable and unsafe for CT → bedside **echo**; high suspicion/delayed imaging → anticoagulate
★ Most stable VTE → **apixaban/rivaroxaban**; pregnancy → LMWH; severe renal failure → UFH
Lysis contraindicated/fails → catheter thrombectomy/surgical embolectomy; active intracranial bleeding precludes lysis
Acute proximal DVT/PE + absolute anticoagulation contraindication → temporary **IVC filter**, remove when feasible

rows.label: Complications
items: Postthrombotic syndrome; persistent dyspnea → evaluate chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
Anticoagulation/thrombolysis → bleeding; heparin → HIT

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Major transient trigger → **3 months** anticoagulation; unprovoked/persistent risk → extended course if low bleeding risk
Hospital prophylaxis: LMWH; active bleeding → intermittent pneumatic compression; early mobilization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cellulitis: predominantly skin erythema, portal of entry
Ruptured Baker cyst: posterior knee symptoms, cyst on US
Pneumonia: focal infiltrate and infectious prodrome
